title: Slot Synthesis Simulator and SLA Fuzz Playbook
author: Priya Nair
body:
Overview

This playbook describes the Slot Synthesis Simulator (S3) — a reproducible lab harness used to synthesize GPU slot allocation, kernel contention, and scheduler behavior to fuzz-test SLA boundaries. The purpose is to find edge cases where our scheduler, kernel selection, or cache warmup interacts to cause SLO regressions or degraded output fidelity. S3 is intended for benchmarking, pre-release safety gates, and targeted post-incident verification.

Why we built S3

- Production traffic has complex concurrency shapes, prefix-sharing, and mixed model families (FP32/INT8/quantized). Traditional replay and unit microbenchmarks miss combinatorial scheduling interactions.
- S3 allows us to simulate: heterogeneous accelerators, slot preemption, admission spikes, varying sequence length distributions, and KV-cache warmup patterns.
- Results feed into kernel/operator rollouts, scheduler policy tuning, and gating decisions for quantization/feature releases.

Glossary

- slot: logical GPU allocation unit used by the scheduler (can map to CUDA context / compute slice).
- slot synthesis: creating synthetic slot occupancy patterns over time to emulate real request mixes.
- SLO fuzz: intentionally varying traffic and system parameters beyond expected ranges to find brittle decision boundaries.
- fidelity cliff: abrupt quality degradation (latency or output) when scheduler or kernel changes occur.

High-level architecture of S3

1) Input generator: consumes a workload profile (sequence-length histogram, model mix, KV-cache hit curves) and emits a timeline of synthetic requests.
2) Slot modeler: maps requests to slot occupancy using configurable policies (co-location, isolation, preemption windows).
3) Kernel stressor: simulates kernel handoffs, warm/cold kernel latencies, and queueing at kernel dispatcher granularity.
4) Metrics sink: collects per-request synthetic metrics (simulated service time, queue delay), aggregates into SLO windows, and emits experiment reports.

Simulator configuration reference (key fields)

- experiment_name: short id for the run
- duration_seconds: wall-clock duration of the simulation
- models: ordered list of model stubs with per-model latency and token-cost distributions
- slot_topology: definition of slot counts, types (cpu, gpu_a100, gpu_h100, tpu), and heterogeneity mapping
- admission_policy: policy id (e.g., conservative, balanced, aggressive) to exercise scheduler branches
- preemption_profile: probability/time-window parameters to synthesize preemption events
- kv_warmup_curve: mapping from time to hit-rate for prefix cache
- sequence_length_distribution: empirical histogram or parametric (p95, mean)

Sample YAML experiment (copy/paste into simulator CLI)

---
experiment_name: "s3_sla_fuzz_canary_2026_02"
duration_seconds: 3600
models:
  - name: "lm-medium-quant"
    mean_token_ms: 6.8
    token_std_ms: 1.2
    kv_sensitivity: 1.6  # relative slowdown when kv miss
  - name: "chat-large"
    mean_token_ms: 12.3
    token_std_ms: 3.1
    kv_sensitivity: 1.0
slot_topology:
  - type: "gpu_h100"
    count: 8
    slots_per_gpu: 4
  - type: "gpu_a100"
    count: 12
    slots_per_gpu: 2
admission_policy: "balanced"
preemption_profile:
  probability: 0.08
  min_interval_ms: 5000
  max_drain_ms: 12000
kv_warmup_curve: "linear:0.2->0.85:900"
sequence_length_distribution: "empirical:seq_hist_2026_q1.json"
---

CLI examples

- Dry run (no metric sink):
  ./s3 run --config examples/canary.yaml --dry-run

- Full run with metrics upload: 
  ./s3 run --config examples/canary.yaml --metrics gs://redwood-s3/experiments/2026/

Primary metrics and acceptance criteria

- p50 / p95 / p99 tail latency (per-model and global) — baseline delta tolerated: p95 <= baseline_p95 * 1.15 for a non-blocking release; p95 <= baseline_p95 * 1.05 for a kernel rollout gate.
- SLO violation rate (requests exceeding latency SLO) — gating threshold: < 0.5% for general release, < 0.1% for high-risk kernel changes.
- Queue growth rate: slope of queue length over 60s windows (alert if > 15 req/s/min sustained).
- Preemption-induced failure probability: fraction of preempted requests that miss deadline (>1% requires investigation).
- Cost signal (simulated GPU-seconds): used to catch regression in per-token cost.

Experiment recipes (start here depending on intent)

1) Canary kernel rollout simulation (safety gate)
   - Purpose: measure effect of new kernel variant on tail latency under mixed traffic.
   - Steps: pick production model mix; set 10% of slots to new_kernel profile; run S3 for 1 hour with several admission_policy values (conservative, balanced, aggressive); compare per-model p99 and p95 to baseline.
   - Gate: no model-level p99 regression > 10% and global SLO violation < 0.1%.

2) Affinity breakdown stress test
   - Purpose: validate slot co-location rules under hot-model concentration.
   - Steps: synthesize a hot-spot where 30% of requests target a single model; force co-location policy to pack slots; inject KV cache cold start at t=0.
   - Gate: queue growth rate must stabilize within 120s. If not, mark admission_policy for tuning.

3) Preemption fuzz (edge-case discovery)
   - Purpose: discover corner cases where preemption ordering and kernel handoffs cause starvation.
   - Steps: set preemption_profile.probability to 0.2 and reduce min_interval_ms to 1000; run for 30 minutes and log any request hitting >2x latency SLO.
   - Gate: debug any observed requests, capture decision traces and slot assignment timeline.

Runbook: executing a baseline S3 experiment

1) Prepare baseline artifacts: workload profile, seq_hist, and baseline_p95 numbers (from production telemetry).
2) Upload config to experiments bucket and mark experiment_name with owner prefix (e.g., se-runtime/alice-s3-2026-02).
3) Start dry-run locally to validate config: ./s3 run --config ... --dry-run.
4) Run full experiment with metrics sink.
5) Publish report: include aggregated graphs, regression table (models vs baseline), and raw traces link.
6) If failure gates hit, open a bug in JIRA and tag owner_team: eng-serving-runtime.

Safety and preconditions (must be satisfied before risky runs)

- All kernel rollout experiments must be run with a baseline reference and known-good commit id.
- Long-running fuzz runs (>6h) must be signed off by the runtime lead and scheduled to avoid infra contention.
- Secrets and PII: S3 must never be run with production user data; use anonymized or synthetic request shapes only.

Interpreting S3 outputs

- Regression matrix: rows = models, cols = metrics (p50/p95/p99, SLO rate, cost). Flag cells that exceed gate thresholds.
- Decision trace artifacts: a sequence of slot assignment events + kernel hints. Use the trace viewer (link in appendix) to step through abnormal requests.
- Heatmaps: slot occupancy over time; look for correlated increases in kernel queue time and KV-miss spikes.

Common failure modes and troubleshooting checklist

- Symptom: p99 regressions concentrated on quantized models
  - Likely cause: kv_sensitivity underestimation or inadequate kernel warmup for INT8 kernels.
  - Actions: increase kv_warmup_curve, re-run GPU affinity packing test.

- Symptom: sustained queue growth under "balanced" policy
  - Likely cause: admission_policy implementation mismatch with production (policy parameters differ).
  - Actions: export production admission snapshot, reconcile parameter differences, re-run.

- Symptom: flakiness between runs (non-deterministic results)
  - Likely cause: RNG seeds not pinned or sequence_length_distribution referencing mutable live corpus.
  - Actions: pin seeds in config and use archived seq_hist files.

Ownership and escalation

- S3 maintainer: runtime-simulations@redwood (primary: Priya Nair)
- Escalation path: if experiment shows SLO regressions that could impact customers, notify runtime-oncall -> eng-sre -> product-security if customer data concerns.

Appendix A — Example regression report table (text)

Model | baseline_p95_ms | experiment_p95_ms | delta% | gate_pass
----- | --------------- | ----------------- | -----: | :-----:
lm-medium-quant | 150 | 163 | 8.7% | PASS
chat-large | 320 | 365 | 14.1% | FAIL
reranker-small | 90 | 95 | 5.6% | PASS

Appendix B — Debugging commands and artifacts

- Capture decision trace id from experiment report and open viewer: http://internal-trace-viewer/trace/<TRACE_ID>
- Convert a trace to CSV for offline analysis: ./s3 export-trace --id <TRACE_ID> --format csv --out /tmp/trace.csv
- Run a focused synthetic microbursts test to reproduce: ./s3 run --config examples/microburst.yaml --duration 600

Appendix C — Known limitations of S3

- S3 models kernel cost and queueing but does not currently simulate low-level GPU thermal throttling; regressions caused by temperature-induced frequency scaling must be validated on hardware labs.
- Network cross-node RPC timing variance is approximated; multi-node scatter/gather effects should be validated with shadow traffic tests.
